vulnerable_statements.reason: RX URBs are submitted to the USB core during the init stage of probe, before the rest of the device setup (e.g. chip info/core init, ieee80211 registration) has completed. If a later probe step fails, the error path frees rtwdev/rtwusb and the workqueue without killing these in-flight URBs. Their completion handlers (and the queued rx_work) can then run against freed memory, which is a use-after-free. Teardown also does not kill them before the workqueue is destroyed.

suggested_fix: Split RX setup into two steps. rtw_usb_init_rx should only allocate the workqueue, the skb queue and the work item. A separate rtw_usb_setup_rx should submit the RX URBs, and it should run only after probe has fully succeeded (after ieee80211 registration). On every probe-failure and disconnect path, kill all RX URBs (usb_kill_urb), then cancel or flush rx_work, then destroy the workqueue, before any rtwdev/rtwusb memory is freed.
